PART I ANALYSIS FOR SILVER AND COPPER

0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part I) was adopted by the Indian Standards
Institution on 14 June 1968, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 For the correct analysis of copper-phosphorus brazing alloys, which are mainly used for joining copper and copper alloys, certain methods In this part, the methods for have been laid down in this standard. analysis of silver and copper have been prescribed. The method for the determination of phosphorus is being investigated and will be covered in Part IL of this standard. 0.3 In the formulation of this standard, due weightage has been given to international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. This has been met by deriving assistance from the c 1967 Book of ASTM Methods for chemical analysis of metals: Part 32 ' issued by the American Society for Testing and Materials. 0.4 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard

(Part I ) prescribes methods for chemical of silver and copper in various grades of copper-phosphorus alloys as specified in IS : 2927-1964t.

4. DETERMINATION

OF SILVER BY THE GRAVIMETRIC

METHOD 4.1 Outline of the Method - The sample is dissolved in nitric acid and silver precipitated as silver chloride by means of hydrochloric acid. The precipitate is filterrd, washed, dried and weighed.
4.2 Reagents

4.2.1 Dilute Nitric Acid 4.2.2 Dilute Hydrochloric 4.3 Procedure

1 : 1 and 3 : 97 ( V/V). Acid 1 : 9 ( v/v).

4.3.1 Transfer 2 g of an accurately weighed sample into a 250-ml Add 25 ml of dilute nitric acid ( 1 : 1 ). Heat gently to beaker. d&solve and boil to remove the brown fumes. Cool to room temperature and dilute to 50 ml.
4.3.2 Add 25 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid ( 1 : 9 ) slowly with consLet it stand for about an hour. tant stirring. 4.3.3 Decant the solution through a weighed sintered glass crucible. Wash the precipitate with warm dilute nitric acid ( 3 : 97 ) till free from chloride and decant through the crucible. Transfer the filtrate and washings to a 400-ml beaker and reserve for the determination of copper. 4.3.4 Dry the crucible and precipitate at about a desiccator to room temperature and reweigh. 4.4 Calculation Silver, where A = weight in g of silver chloride, and B = weight in g of the sample taken. *Specification for water, distilled quality ( revised ). 4 percent = A x 75.26 B 110�C. CYLINDRICAL PLATINUM CATHODE AND SPIRAL PLATINUM ANODE

5.2.1.1 Gauze cathodes, made preferably from gauze containing 400 mesh/ems, should be used. The wire used for making gauze should be approximately O-20 mm in diameter. Cathodes should be stiffened by doubling the gauze for about 3 mm on the top and bottom or by reinforcing the gauze at the top and bottom with platinum ring or band.

5

IS:4646(PartI)-1968 5.2.1.2 The diameter and height of the cylinder should be approximately 30and 50 mm respectively. The stem should be made from platinum alloy wire, such as platinum-iridium, platinum-rhodium or platinum-ruthenium having diameter approximately 1.5 mm. It should be flattened and welded to the entire height of the gauze. The overall height of the cathode including the stem should approximately be 130 mm.
5.2.2 Anode - Either a spiral or a gauze anode should be used. The spiral anode should be made from l-O-mm or larger platinum wire formed into a spiral of seven coils with a height approximately 50 mm and diameter 12 mm, the overall height including the stem being 130 mm. The gauze anode should be made of the same material and of the same general design as platinum gauze cathode specified under 5.2.1. 5.3 Reagents 1961* ).

5.4 Procedure

5.4.1 To the filtrate and washings reserved under 4.3.3, add 5 ml .of concentrated sulphuric acid and evaporate to fumes. Cool, dilute to 250 ml and add 10 ml of concentrated nitric acid.
5.4.2 Weigh the cathode, adjust the electrodes in the solution, and cover with a pair of split watch-glasses. Add 2 g of urea. Electrolyze at a current density of 0.6 A/dm8 ( at this current density, the electrolysis is conveniently carried on overnight ), or at a current density of 4 A/dma for a short period ( about 2'5 hours ). In the latter case, one of the types of rotating forms of electrodes generally available may be used. When the solution becomes colourless, reduce the current density to 03 A/dms and continue electrolysis until the deposition of copper is complete as indicated by failure of copper to plate on the newly exposed cathode surface when the solution level is raised. *Specification for sulphurio acid ( revised). tSpecifioationfor nitric acid. 6

IS : 4646 ( Part I ) - 1968 5.4.3 Without interrupting the current, lower the beaker slowly while rinsing the electrodes with water and collecting the washings Remove the cathode quickly, rinse it with in the electrolyte. water in a beaker and then dip it in two successive baths of ethanol or Dry the cathode in an air oven at 110�C for three to five methanol. The difference in weight gives minutes, cool and reweigh the cathode. the weight of copper deposited.
